translation: I am a dwarf.
analysis: Hamarkor is a predicate noun; no occupational implication.

translation: We are dwarves.
analysis: Plural predicate noun; verb does not agree.

translation: The stoneworker builds the chamber.
Now I build the chamber.

text: Na da kelum vare da menir.
translation: The stoneworker speaks inside the chamber.
analysis: Whole location phrase occupies first field.

translation: Do you build the chamber?
Who builds the chamber?
What do you build?
Where is the child?
With whom do you speak?
I do not build the chamber.

text: Nu have ek ne karnet da kel.
translation: Now I have not built the chamber.

text: Ek vare ke sa ne karne da kel.
translation: I say that they do not build the chamber.
analysis: Singular sa; dependent negation before finite.

text: Ek vite se du karne da kel.
translation: I know whether you build the chamber.

text: Ek vite hor du karne da kel.
translation: I know where you build the chamber.

text: Da kor ri karne da kel sere her.
translation: The person who builds the chamber is here.
analysis: Relative subject gap; entire noun phrase precedes main copula.

text: Da kel ri ek karne sere storr.
translation: The chamber that I build is large.
analysis: Relative object gap; predicate adjective remains uninflected.

text: Da kor ri ek vare me saum sere her.
translation: The person with whom I speak is here.

text: Da kor ri ne karne da kel sere her.
translation: The person who does not build the chamber is here.
analysis: Subject gap followed by ne + finite.

translation: My chamber is here.
The stoneworker's chamber is here.

text: Ek have kel af da menirum.
translation: I have a chamber belonging to the stoneworker.
analysis: Bare head plus postposed association phrase.

text: Ek give da men til duum.
translation: I give the stone to you.
They wash themself.
analysis: Singular reflexive refers to clause subject.

translation: They wash another person referred to as they.
analysis: Distinct third-person referent; repeat names if unclear.

translation: They have their own hand hammer.
They have another person's hand hammer.
We help one another.

text: Ek vare me sium ak duum.
translation: I speak with myself and you.
analysis: Reflexive sium is clause-subject-bound; both conjuncts carry oblique.

text: Da men sere darn ak spröd.
translation: The stone is scratch-resistant and brittle.

text: Di men sere mer darn dan dan men.
translation: This stone is harder than that stone.
analysis: First dan is comparison linker; second is determiner.

text: Di kel sere sam storr as dan kel.
translation: This chamber is as large as that chamber.
analysis: Sam + adjective + as introduces an equal comparison.

translation: The stoneworker built the nursery.
I have built the chamber.
I had built the chamber.
I will build the chamber.

text: Ek fere haven karnet da kel.
translation: I will have built the chamber.
I can carry the stone.
I must remain silent.
analysis: Positive obligation with lexical silent verb.

translation: I am not obliged to speak.
I prohibit speaking.
analysis: Activity infinitive; not I must not speak.

text: Ek love ke da ner ete.
translation: I permit the child to eat.

text: Da kel vere karnet af da menirum.
translation: The chamber is being built by the stoneworker.
The chamber stands built.
I am now engaged in building.

text: Vel da drav stane, stane da rad.
translation: If the water flow stops, the wheel stops.
analysis: Dependent clause fills first main-clause field.

text: Vel ek vu havte da men, fere ek vu karnen da kel.
translation: If I had the stone, I would build the chamber.
analysis: Vu has documented dependent and main positions.

translation: I come to help.

text: Ek karne da kel te ke da ner mage soven.
translation: I build the chamber so that the child can sleep.
analysis: Te ke introduces explicit new subject.

text: Tem da kel, ek karne di.
translation: As for the chamber, I build it.
Do not open the door.

text: Bitte, giv da men til ekum.
translation: Please give the stone to me.

text: Pom da vas in da dravkelum.
translation: Pump the water into the cistern.
The water flow powers the wheel.
I test the sample.
analysis: Tröv and trov remain different words.

text: Ek merke da trov me markum.
translation: I label the sample with a mark.

text: Da gred af stalmenum sere ne vitet.
translation: The support-stone grade is not known.
analysis: Explicit lack of knowledge; not a failed grade.

translation: The sample is dry, by observation.

text: Ek tönke ke da trov sere tör.
translation: I think the sample is dry.
analysis: Thought complement rather than asserted measurement.

text: Da egg sere na da eggkelum.
translation: The egg is inside the egg compartment.

text: Da ner sere na da nerkelum.
translation: The child is in the nursery.
analysis: No claim that the child is itself a geode.

translation: I care for and protect the child.

text: Ek sele da ner me selum.
translation: I feed the child with nourishment.
analysis: Recipient is direct object; food is me phrase.

translation: The child holds the hand hammer.
I want water.
I eat the tuber.
analysis: Food object of eten; functional crop analog rather than an Earth species.

translation: I like the fungal food.
I love you.
I grieve.
The child plays.
We sing the song.
I have no stone.
analysis: Neng already makes a negative quantity.

translation: Two chambers are here.

text: Ek take tor kapar af vasum.
translation: I take two vessel-units of water.

text: Da kel sere höl ak dypp.
translation: The chamber is high and deeply covered.
analysis: Two independent spatial properties with contextual datums.

translation: I travel sunward.
analysis: Adverb, not preposition requiring a case.

translation: I travel through the tunnel.

text: Vite du se da vas drave?
translation: Do you know whether the water flows?
I want to learn Common Dwarven.

text: Ek läre Korvar til da nerum.
translation: I teach Common Dwarven to the child.
analysis: Content object; learner as explicit recipient.

translation: Hello. Can you help me?
Yes. What do you want?
analysis: Yes response distinct from clause negation.

translation: I want two dressed stone pieces.
I give these to you.
analysis: Di resumes the previously requested plural stones.

translation: Thanks. I will pay.
Farewell.

text: Eks helm sere na da bergum.
translation: My home is inside the mountain.

text: Da kel sere höl, dar da kammeel sere kurt.
translation: The chamber is high, but the rock cover is shallow.
analysis: Literal cover thickness is short; elevation is a separate quantity.

translation: The water flow powers the wheel.
We have fungal food and tubers.
analysis: Food sources; no assertion of underground primary production.

text: Na da nerkelum sove da ner.
translation: The child sleeps in the nursery.

text: Nu vare ek me da rukkorum.
translation: Now I speak with the caregiver.
analysis: Care role with explicit oblique phrase.

translation: I have a piece of dark fine-grained rock.
analysis: Count reading of the natural rock category.

text: Da rak sere darn ak spröd.
translation: The rock is scratch-resistant and brittle.

text: Da gred af stalmenum sere ne vitet.
translation: Its support-stone grade is not known.
I will test the sample.
analysis: Future action, not a fabricated result.

text: Eft fere ek skriven da döm.
translation: Afterward I will write the decision.
Now we must wait.
analysis: Positive obligation in a connected technical exchange.
